title: Mock server test pattern may break if hyper changes response parsing
description:
Integration tests (integration.rs lines 24-41) spawn a mock that writes raw HTTP/1.1 bytes and closes immediately. Tests assume hyper will:
  1. Parse the response as valid HTTP/1.1
  2. Not retry or re-negotiate on socket close
  3. Return body to the caller before detecting connection close

RISK: If hyper changes how it handles connection closure during response body streaming, these tests might pass while real tailscaled interaction breaks (or vice versa).

ISSUE: Mock server is too simple — it doesn't replicate tailscaled behavior (persistent connection, proper HTTP state machine).

SUGGESTION: Consider using a real minimal HTTP server (http-crate or simple-server) that keeps connections alive, or add a comment explaining why the raw-write pattern is adequate.
